[[Treasure]] refers to a special type of unlocked [[chest]] found in the [[Nightfall]] campaign.

== Names ==
*[[Buried Treasure]]
*[[Do Not Touch]]
*[[Treasure Chest]]

== Contents ==
Opening treasure yields both a single item ([[drop]]ped on the ground) and some [[Currency|gold]] (added directly to your [[character]]'s [[inventory]]). The item will be either a [[weapon]] or a [[salvage item]] (of [[item rarity|gold or purple rarity]]), or a gem ([[diamond]], [[ruby]] or [[sapphire]]). As with other loot, the drops are more valuable in the areas further into the story. The initial cash value ranges from about 500{{gold}} in [[Istan]] to 3,000{{gold}} in the [[Realm of Torment]]. A player might expect to receive 20{{plat}} on the first few times they open every treasure for each character. The drop quality however decreases on subsequent openings; see [[#Notes|Notes]] for more information.

== Notes ==
* Treasures are always unlocked. Neither [[key]]s nor [[lockpick]]s are required.
* Treasures labeled ''Do Not Touch'' often are guarded by several hidden [[Immolated Djinn|Immolated]] or [[Ruby Djinn]] that will [[popup]] when the treasure is opened. Spread your [[party]] out before opening to avoid their dangerous [[area of effect]] skills.

; Treasure quality

''Treasure quality'' is the gold reward amount and the type and rarity of the item(s) found in the treasure. The factors governing quality are not entirely understood; however, the following properties have been well documented:

* Gold quantities are linked to the rarity of items drops: purple item drops reward about {{2/3}} the amount of gold as compared to gold item drops.
* Quality decreases permanently for a character each time they reveal any treasure.<ref name="Joe Kimmes on Nightfall Treasure">https://wiki.guildwars.com/index.php?title=Feedback_talk:Joe_Kimmes&diff=next&oldid=2228651#Nightfall_Treasure</ref>
** The lower gold limits appear to be as little as 100{{gold}} in Istan and 700{{gold}} in the Realm of Torment, or around 20% of the original value on average once the scaling reaches its lowest point.
** Scaling of the rewards only kicks in after a particular number of treasures (significantly more than three) have been revealed,<ref>https://wiki.guildwars.com/index.php?title=Feedback_talk%3AJoe_Kimmes&diff=2260537&oldid=2260468</ref> and levels out after another number of the treasures have been opened.<ref name="Joe Kimmes on Nightfall Treasure">https://wiki.guildwars.com/index.php?title=Feedback_talk:Joe_Kimmes&diff=next&oldid=2228651#Nightfall_Treasure</ref>
** As a rule of thumb, in the beginning all [[weapon]] and [[salvage item]] drops are [[item rarity|gold rarity]], and once the minimum treasure quality has been reached all are [[item rarity|purple]].
* [[Hard mode]] does not appear to affect the values.

; Treasure availability
Each character can receive loot only once during a certain period, believed to be around 30 days per treasure. Opening the chest too soon means that there will be no treasure; some evidence suggests that this resets the waiting period. Obtaining treasure from a chest also appears to reset the waiting period for that character as a whole.

{{anomaly|Sometimes opening treasure yields a single gold rarity item but no gold.<!--[[Talk:Treasure#Gold...and No Gold]]-->}}
